6,000 simulated seasons, KickTip blendSimulation analysis, not advice. Data as of Nov 21, 6:59 PM MT.

Each number is Texas State’s chance if that side wins the game. KickTip runs 6,000 simulated seasons with that one game decided each way, using the same simulator as What If Lab by KickTip.

Every other game is simulated as usual. The points are the difference between the two results, so the bigger the difference, the more that game matters to Texas State.

Each game is tested on its own. Do not add the points together: results of different games overlap.

Games that move the chance by less than 1 pt are not shown. Small differences can come from simulation noise.

These numbers use 6,000 seasons, so they can differ by a few tenths from the 10,000-season chances shown above.

Rootables uses the rating system selected above. Change the rating system and the list updates.

How to read these numbers. The ESPN spread shows the team ESPN expects to win and by how many points, with a minus sign: Utah −3.0 means ESPN has Utah winning by 3.0. KickTip's expected margin is our own estimate: the team KickTip expects to win and by how many points, for example “Utah by 3.5” (rounded to 0.5 on the page). The ESPN spread is shown with the time it was read (MT) and only when ESPN has posted one. Neither number is a recommendation. Information only.

Games against FCS opponents are counted in the simulation but have no ESPN spread or expected margin.
